policy: Complete for the explicitly stated source catalog and retained legacy examples, not an assertion of every possible real-world item. Sources may change after this snapshot. Canonical source labels and supporting URLs are factual evidence, not copied source prose.

git-commands.scope: All command entries in the Git 2.56 command manual retrieved 2026-11-23, including porcelain, plumbing and documented helper commands. Options and guide names do not count. Accept the subcommand with or without git.

linux-commands.scope: Every section-1 user-command entry in the man7.org Linux manual index retrieved 2026-11-23; a command with several manual entries counts once. Shell builtins already accepted by the game remain accepted.

programming-languages.scope: All GitHub Linguist entries typed programming, plus entries whose canonical name contains SQL, from the 2026-11-23 registry snapshot. Registry aliases count. Markup, prose and unrelated data formats are excluded. Previously accepted engineering-language names remain accepted.

nasa.scope: Every entry in NASA’s A to Z List of NASA Missions snapshot retrieved 2026-11-23. The directory also includes NASA-supported international missions, instruments, experiments and technology programs, which count. Numbered missions are separate from their umbrella program; previously accepted spacecraft also remain accepted.

famous-engineers.scope: Every inductee in the National Inventors Hall of Fame’s full alphabetic list retrieved 2026-11-23. This replaces the former unbounded famous engineer/inventor/scientist question. Honorary groups and fictional people are excluded.

polygons.scope: Every numeric polygon in the names table on MathWorld’s Polygon page (2–20 sides, multiples of ten through 100, and 10,000), plus the originally accepted named shapes/large polygons. An n-gon spelling is an alias only for listed side counts. This finite reference list replaces the former unbounded wording.

bridge-types.scope: Every named structure type in Table 10 of FHWA’s LTBP Bridge Performance Primer (Other excluded), together with originally accepted bridge designs, uses and movable-bridge types. The explicit finite reference list is the scope; materials and arbitrary combinations are not extra answers.

engineering-majors.scope: Every distinct bachelor’s major in the College of Engineering’s Degree Programs Offered directory retrieved 2026-11-23. BS/BA versions and departmental duplicates share one major answer. Graduate degrees, minors, concentrations and certificates are excluded.

circuit-components.scope: Every one of the 564 generic symbols in KiCad’s Device library retrieved 2026-11-23 is covered by a component-family answer; package, pin-order, drawing-style and channel-count variants share a family. Previously accepted ICs, sensors and other circuit components also count. Symbol identifiers are accepted aliases.

metals.scope: All elements in PubChem’s Alkali metal, Alkaline earth metal, Transition metal, Post-transition metal, Lanthanide and Actinide groups as retrieved 2026-11-23, plus the originally accepted alloy families. Metalloids/nonmetals and arbitrary commercial grades are excluded. Element symbols are accepted only when unambiguous.

hand-tools.scope: All tool families and named variants in the List of Tools in Army TM 9-867 Maintenance and Care of Hand Tools, plus previously accepted modern hand tools. A family may group minor variants; the full names of those variants are aliases. Abrasive wheels, oilstones, measuring tools and manual accessories in the source list count.

airplane-parts.scope: All airplane component labels/families in FAA Pilot’s Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, Chapter 3 Aircraft Construction, plus the originally accepted aircraft parts and named subcomponents in the published reference list. Aircraft categories, aerodynamic forces and construction materials do not count as parts.

engineering-failures.scope: Every completed investigation listed across all 20 pages of the U.S. Chemical Safety Board directory retrieved 2026-11-23, plus the original aviation, space, nuclear, structural and other engineering case studies. Multiple reports on one incident share one answer. A disaster being included does not imply that every death or impact was caused only by an engineering error.
